Local paper asked to interview my college Veterans Club on the NFL issue, and I got asked to be the one to do it. Any words of wisdom?
Record the entire thing so you can't be misrepresented.

Start with a written statement that encompasses all the obvious questions. You can hand it to the interviewer and elaborate on anything from there. This way you'll have a well articulated stance without running the risk of misspeaking. Other than that don't get too emotional. Find a well articulated position and defend it.

I don't want to put words in your mouth but some things that you should think about
-What does the flag represent to you
-Does being a vet give you any sort of special licence here
-Are you more concerned about the content of their speech or how they are delivering it
-What other methods would you suggest for these people to express themselves
-What obligation does the NFL have to protect it's image (or shudder promote social issues) and how does this compare to being a service member/college student
-If you previously enjoyed the NFL, why? (not saying that you should or shouldn't but this is a good thing to think about as it's a natural bridge between the players and the fans)
-How would this situation be different if the players were protesting something that you are passionate about even if you disagreed with the way the protest was conducted
